cor-ply-sequential.title: Fitting in the orthonormal basis
cor-ply-sequential.html:
Let qj have entries qj(xi) and let the weights be one, so the qj are orthonormal in Rn; write γ^j=qj⊤y. For every d<m:

  1. the least squares fit of degree d is f^d(t)=∑j=0dγ^jqj(t), and γ^j does not depend on d;

  2. E(γ^j)=⟨f,qj⟩ when E(Yi)=f(xi) for any function f, and 𝛄Cov(γ^)=σ2I;

  3. the residual sum of squares equals ‖y‖2−∑j≤dγ^j2, so the sequential sum of squares for degree j is γ^j2 on one degree of freedom, free of the order of entry;

  4. the F statistic for H:γd=0 in the model of degree d is γ^d2/σ^d2, with σ^d2 that model’s residual mean square, on (1,n−d−1) degrees of freedom.

def-ply-orthogonal.title: Orthogonal polynomials for a design
def-ply-orthogonal.html: Let x1,…,xn be design points, m of them distinct, with weights w1,…,wn>0. For real functions f,g on the design write ⟨f,g⟩=∑i=1nwif(xi)g(xi),‖f‖2=⟨f,f⟩, an inner product on the functions restricted to the design. Polynomials p0,…,pd with d<m are the orthogonal polynomials of the design if pj has degree exactly j with leading coefficient one (it is monic) and ⟨pj,pk⟩=0 for j≠k. The normalized qj=pj/‖pj‖ are the orthonormal polynomials of the design.

def-ply-piecewise.title: Piecewise polynomials and continuity constraints
def-ply-piecewise.html:
Fix an interval [a,b] and knots a=κ0<κ1<⋯<κK<κK+1=b, the K inner ones being the interior knots. A function f:[a,b]→R is a piecewise polynomial of degree d if its restriction to each half-open piece [κk,κk+1), k=0,…,K−1, and to [κK,b] agrees with a polynomial of degree at most d; the value at a knot is the limit from the right, and nothing ties the pieces together. These form a vector space PPd(κ) of dimension (K+1)(d+1).

For −1≤m≤d−1, f satisfies the continuity constraints of order m at κk if f(r)(κk−)=f(r)(κk+),r=0,1,…,m, the case m=−1 imposing nothing. The spline space Sd(κ) is the set of piecewise polynomials of degree d satisfying the constraints of order d−1 at every interior knot; its members are the splines of degree d with knots κ.

def-ply-polynomial.title: Polynomial regression
def-ply-polynomial.html: Let x1,…,xn be observed values of a single regressor. The polynomial regression model of degree d is E(Yi)=β0+β1xi+β2xi2+⋯+βdxid,i=1,…,n, a linear model with the n×(d+1) Vandermonde matrix X=[1,x,x2,…,xd], where xj has entries xij. More generally, any functions ϕ0,…,ϕd give columns ϕj(x) and a fitted curve f^(t)=∑jβ^jϕj(t); they are a basis, and the model is the space Pd=span{ϕ0,…,ϕd}, not the list.

def-ply-regression-spline.title: Regression spline
def-ply-regression-spline.html: Given a degree d and fixed interior knots κ1<⋯<κK inside the range of the design, the regression spline model is the linear model with model matrix X=[1, x, …, xd, (x−κ1)+d, …, (x−κK)+d], of d+1+K columns, and the regression spline is the least squares fit 𝛃f^(t)=x(t)⊤β^. Other regressors, smooth terms and factors may be added as further columns.

eq-ply-recurrence.html: p−1=0,p0=1,pj+1(x)=(x−aj)pj(x)−bjpj−1(x),j=0,1,…,d−1,

eq-ply-truncated.html: 1, t, …, td, (t−κ1)+d, …, (t−κK)+d

exm-ply-co2-degree.title: Degree in the carbon dioxide series
exm-ply-co2-degree.title_html: Degree in the carbon dioxide series
exm-ply-co2-degree.html:
The monthly mean carbon dioxide at Mauna Loa, March 1958 to December 2001, gives n=521 observations; @exm-lm-co2 modelled it with a quadratic trend and two seasonal harmonics. Keep the four harmonic columns and replace the quadratic by a polynomial of degree d in time rescaled to [−1,1]. The residual standard deviation falls from 0.7602 ppm at d=2 (p=7) to 0.4874 at d=8 and 0.4300 at d=16, while no harmonic coefficient moves by more than 0.0150 ppm.

The improvement is real: panel (a) of Figure 42.1.1 shows the residuals of the quadratic fit wandering by a part per million over decades, and the higher-degree trends tracking that wandering. The price is in panel (b). In the middle of the range the standard error of the fitted mean is much the same at all three degrees — 0.0830, 0.0676, 0.0730 ppm at 1980 — but at the left-hand edge it is 0.1217, 0.2011, 0.2899, so the ratio of edge to centre rises from 1.47 to 2.97 to 3.97. Leverages tell the same story: average 0.0134, 0.0250, 0.0403 against maximum 0.0256, 0.1702, 0.4546. At degree 16 one month, the first of the series, carries almost half of its own fitted value.

exm-ply-co2-spline.title: Trend bases for the carbon dioxide series
exm-ply-co2-spline.title_html: Trend bases for the carbon dioxide series
exm-ply-co2-spline.html:
Return to the n=521 monthly means with the four seasonal columns fixed, put K=6 interior knots at the quantiles k/7 of the time variable, and compare six trend bases.

Trend basis p Residual SS σ^ GCV maxhii
quadratic 7 297.03 0.7602 0.5858 0.0256
degree 9 14 115.57 0.4774 0.2343 0.2054
degree 16 21 92.44 0.4300 0.1926 0.4546
piecewise constant 11 3081.18 2.4580 6.1718 0.0215
piecewise linear 12 116.63 0.4787 0.2345 0.0532
cubic spline 14 108.48 0.4626 0.2199 0.1494

Read the middle rows against each other. At the same p=14 the cubic spline fits better than the degree-9 polynomial (108.48 against 115.57) and spreads its influence more evenly (largest leverage 0.1494 against 0.2054); panel (a) of Figure 42.4.1 shows the two parting where the polynomial has to bend. The step function is a disaster; the broken line is almost as good as the cubic spline with two fewer parameters, at the cost of visible kinks (panel (b)).

In-sample, GCV prefers the degree-16 polynomial to everything else (0.1926) — honest about prediction at the design points and misleading about the fit, since that model has maxhii=0.4546 and κ(X)=5.39×105. Among the piecewise bases the cubic spline is the worst conditioned: κ(X)=7.72×103 against 9.75×101.

exm-ply-extrapolation.title: Eleven years out of sample
exm-ply-extrapolation.html: Fit the same models to the 389 months up to the end of 1990 and predict the 132 months of 1991–2001. Inside the fitting range the residual standard deviation falls steadily with the degree — 0.439, 0.428, 0.417, 0.406 ppm at degrees 2, 4, 6, 8 — while outside it the root mean squared prediction errors are 3.99, 2.63, 13.92 and 188.23 ppm. The degree-8 fit, the best of the four in-sample, is out by −540.7 ppm in December 2001 against an observed value near 371: it predicts a concentration several hundred parts per million below zero.

exm-ply-knot-placement.title: A skewed design
exm-ply-knot-placement.html:
Take n=200 design points drawn once, with a fixed seed, from a skewed distribution on [0,1], and fit a cubic spline with K=5 interior knots. Equally spaced knots leave 67,71,35,21,5,1 points in the six intervals; quantile knots leave 34,33,33,33,33,34. Both have full rank — the truncated powers are globally supported, so a nearly empty interval does not kill a column — but it does kill precision. The exact pointwise standard deviation of the fit, in units of σ, reaches 7.452 with the equally spaced knots against 0.987 with the quantile knots; at the median of the design the quantile knots are slightly worse (0.173 against 0.123), having spent four of five knots there.

Quantile knots are a defensible default, not a universal optimum: they make the worst case tolerable. Where the regression function is known to vary fast in a sparse region the knots should follow the function — a choice made from outside the data, or paid for as a selection (@prp-sel-selection-bias).

exm-ply-nile-ladder.title: Four fits with the same knots
exm-ply-nile-ladder.title_html: Four fits with the same knots
exm-ply-nile-ladder.html:
Take the Nile series again, n=100 annual flows, with cubic pieces and interior knots at 1899 — where Cobb (1978) and the analysis of @exm-ss-nile-polynomials both locate a change — and 1935. Fitting the three cubics separately uses 12 parameters and leaves a residual sum of squares of 1394072. Continuity at both knots removes two parameters and raises it to 1561452; continuity of the first derivative removes two more (1613581); and the full cubic spline, with 6 parameters as @thm-ply-spline-space predicts, has 1781797. Figure 42.3.1 shows the four fits.

Each step down the ladder is a testable linear hypothesis, and against the unrestricted fit all three are rejected: F=5.28 on (2,88) degrees of freedom for continuity alone (p=0.0068), F=3.46 on (4,88) (p=0.0112) for a continuous first derivative, and F=4.08 on (6,88) (p=0.0012) for the cubic spline. The Nile really does have a discontinuity, and a spline is the wrong space for it.

The right model is the simplest on the ladder: a step function with a single knot at 1899, whose group means are 1097.7 and 850.0 in units of 108m3, differing by −247.8 with standard error 28.4 and t=−8.71. Its residual sum of squares, 1597457, beats the six-parameter spline and the cubic polynomial’s 1909955. Two parameters in the right place beat six in the wrong space.

exm-ply-nile-recurrence.title: The recurrence on the Nile series
exm-ply-nile-recurrence.title_html: The recurrence on the Nile series
exm-ply-nile-recurrence.html:
The annual flow of the Nile at Aswan, 1871–1970, gives n=100 equally spaced design points, rescaled here to [−1,1]. @exm-ss-nile-polynomials built its orthonormal polynomials by a QR factorization of the matrix of powers; @eq-ply-recurrence gives the same basis, the largest discrepancy between corresponding columns being 1.1×10−14 and the largest inner product between distinct columns 6.7×10−16, machine precision. The design being symmetric about its mean, every aj vanishes (@exr-ply-symmetric-a), and the first four values of bj are 0.34007, 0.27197, 0.26213, 0.25871; Figure 42.2.1(a) draws the polynomials themselves.

The sequential sums of squares reproduce the table of @exm-ss-nile-polynomials — 613893, 309415, 1894, 134142 for degrees 1 to 4, and 4225 and 7034 for degrees 5 and 6 — with F statistics 27.08, 15.70, 0.10, 7.18, 0.22 and 0.37. The cubic term is negligible and the quartic is not: a reader stopping at the first insignificant term would have missed it.

exm-ply-runge.title: Runge’s function
exm-ply-runge.html: Interpolate f(x)=1/(1+25x2) at m equally spaced points of [−1,1] by the polynomial of degree m−1. The largest error on the interval is 1.92 for m=11, 59.82 for m=21 and 2388.03 for m=31: the function is smooth and bounded by one, and the interpolant does not converge to it. Move the same nodes to the Chebyshev positions cos⁡{(2k+1)π/2m}, which crowd towards the ends, and the errors become 0.10915, 0.01533, 0.00206. Only where the information sits has changed.

exm-ply-truncated-conditioning.title: Truncated powers against a local basis
exm-ply-truncated-conditioning.title_html: Truncated powers against a local basis
exm-ply-truncated-conditioning.html:
For the carbon dioxide design rescaled to [−1,1], take cubic splines with K quantile knots and compare the condition number of the truncated power basis with that of the local (B-spline) basis for the same space, verified by checking that the two sets of columns together have rank K+4.

K 4 8 16 32
truncated powers 1.75×103 2.56×104 3.65×105 4.97×106
local basis 5.30 5.18 5.04 5.00

The truncated power condition number multiplies by about fifteen for every doubling of K; the local basis does not move. By K=32 the normal equations (@thm-proj-normal-equations) in the truncated power basis have lost about thirteen digits (@eq-cmp-rule), the same fit in the local basis one. This design is nearly uniform, so every basis function’s support is well occupied — the proviso of part (d).

exr-ply-add-a-regressor.title: B3
exr-ply-add-a-regressor.html: A model has a cubic spline in x and a linear term in z. Show that the coefficient of z is the slope of the regression of y on the part of z orthogonal to the spline space, and say what it would mean for that part to be nearly zero.

exr-ply-band-honesty.title: B2
exr-ply-band-honesty.html: Compute the pointwise 95% band for the cubic spline fit of @exm-ply-co2-spline and the simultaneous Working–Hotelling band (@thm-ci-working-hotelling). By what factor is the simultaneous band wider, and what does each band cover?

exr-ply-centring-invariance.title: B3
exr-ply-centring-invariance.html: Let u=ax+b1 with a≠0. Show that C([1,u,…,ud])=C([1,x,…,xd]) and that the change of basis matrix is triangular with diagonal entries aj. Deduce that centring and scaling leave Y^, 𝛆ε^ and every leverage unchanged, and say why they nevertheless change κ(X).

exr-ply-degree-invariance.title: A2
exr-ply-degree-invariance.html: A quartic is fitted in the raw powers and again in the orthonormal polynomials of the design. Which of these differ between the two fits: the linear coefficient, the fitted value at x1, the residual sum of squares, the sequential sum of squares for degree 3, the leverage h11, the condition number of X?

exr-ply-derivative-jump.title: B3
exr-ply-derivative-jump.html: Let f∈Sd(κ) have truncated power coefficients θk. Show that f(d) is a step function jumping by d!θk at κk, and that θk=0 exactly when f is a single polynomial across κk.

exr-ply-dimension-count.title: A1
exr-ply-dimension-count.html: How many parameters has a quadratic spline with 7 interior knots? A cubic spline with 7, one of them a double knot (only C1 there)? A piecewise constant function with 7?

exr-ply-equivalent-kernel.title: C1
exr-ply-equivalent-kernel.html: For a regression spline the fitted value at t is ∑iℓi(t)yi with ℓi(t)=x(t)⊤(X⊤X)−1xi. Show that ∑iℓi(t)=1 and ∑iℓi(t)(xi−t)r=0 for r=1,…,d at every t, because Sd(κ) contains Pd and a projection reproduces its own space. Deduce that the fit reproduces polynomials of degree d exactly, and interpret ∑iℓi(t)2.

exr-ply-hat-at-endpoint.title: B2
exr-ply-hat-at-endpoint.html: For the design xi=−1+2(i−1)/(n−1) with n=50, compute the leverage of the leftmost point for d=1,3,…,15 and plot it against d, comparing with the average (d+1)/n and the bound of @prp-proj-leverage.

exr-ply-hilbert.title: B1
exr-ply-hilbert.html: For the design xi=(i−1)/(n−1), show that the (j,k) entry of n−1Xd⊤Xd converges to 1/(j+k+1) for each fixed j,k≤d: part (a) of @prp-ply-instability for a fixed rather than a random design.

exr-ply-influence-polynomial.title: B4
exr-ply-influence-polynomial.html: Verify part (d) of @prp-ply-instability numerically: for the degree-12 trend on the carbon dioxide design compute ℓi(t) for the last observation and count its sign changes over the data, then repeat for d=2. Why is the count for d=2 smaller than 2 in some designs?

exr-ply-knot-coalescence.title: C2
exr-ply-knot-coalescence.html: Let κ and κ+ϵ be two knots of a cubic spline. Show that as ϵ↓0 the angle between (t−κ)+3 and (t−κ−ϵ)+3 tends to zero, while the normalized difference {(t−κ)+3−(t−κ−ϵ)+3}/(3ϵ) tends to (t−κ)+2. Explain how this both shows that a double knot lowers the smoothness by one order and warns against placing knots close together in the truncated power basis.

exr-ply-knot-df.title: A1
exr-ply-knot-df.html: A cubic regression spline with K quantile knots is fitted to n=200 observations together with three other regressors and an intercept. Give the residual degrees of freedom and the average leverage as functions of K, and the K at which the fit interpolates.

exr-ply-knot-selection-cost.title: C2
exr-ply-knot-selection-cost.html: Suppose K minimizes GCV over K∈{1,…,20} and the usual pointwise band is then reported for the selected fit. Simulate 2000 data sets from a known smooth f with normal errors and estimate the coverage of the nominal 95% band at the quartiles of the design, explaining the pattern in terms of @prp-sel-selection-bias and of the bias a selected K leaves behind.

exr-ply-knot-test.title: B1
exr-ply-knot-test.html: Fit cubic splines to the carbon dioxide series with K=2,4,…,20 quantile knots and plot GCV against K, then the leave-one-out criterion computed by the leverage shortcut of @thm-sel-loocv. Where do the two disagree, and why should you not report the F test comparing the selected K with K=2?

exr-ply-lebesgue.title: C2
exr-ply-lebesgue.html: For interpolation at nodes x1<⋯<xm the interpolant is ∑kf(xk)Lk(t), with Lk the Lagrange basis, and the Lebesgue constant is Λ=maxt∑k|Lk(t)|. Show that the interpolation error is at most (1+Λ) times that of the best uniform approximation of degree m−1, compute Λ for m=5,9,13,17 equally spaced and Chebyshev nodes, and relate the two sequences to @exm-ply-runge.

exr-ply-legendre.title: B2
exr-ply-legendre.html: The monic Legendre polynomials are orthogonal for ⟨f,g⟩=∫−11fg. Using @thm-ply-recurrence and the identity ∫−11Pj2=2/(2j+1) for the standard Legendre polynomials, whose leading coefficient is (2jj)2−j, verify that bj=j2/(4j2−1).

exr-ply-natural-dimension.title: B1
exr-ply-natural-dimension.html: Show that the natural cubic splines with interior knots κ1<⋯<κK (K≥2) form a space of dimension K, by writing the four boundary conditions in the truncated power basis and checking that they are independent.

exr-ply-peano.title: C1
exr-ply-peano.html: Show that for f∈Cd+1[a,b], f(t)=∑j=0df(j)(a)j!(t−a)j+1d!∫abf(d+1)(s)(t−s)+dds. Interpret it as saying that the truncated power functions are a continuous basis for smooth functions, of which @eq-ply-truncated keeps K members.

exr-ply-slope-change.title: A2
exr-ply-slope-change.html: In the broken-line model f(t)=β0+β1t+∑kθk(t−κk)+, give the slope of f on (κj,κj+1), the hypothesis that the line is unbent at κj, and the degrees of freedom of the test that it is a single straight line.

exr-ply-step-locality.title: A3
exr-ply-step-locality.html: Verify that for the piecewise constant fit, changing yi by Δ moves the fitted curve by Δ/nk on i’s own interval and not at all elsewhere. Contrast with @prp-ply-instability(d).

exr-ply-storage.title: B3
exr-ply-storage.html: Given a0,…,ad−1, b1,…,bd−1, ‖pj‖2 and γ^0,…,γ^d, write down an algorithm that evaluates f^d(t) at a new t in O(d) operations and storage, without ever computing a power of t. Why is this preferable to expanding f^d in the monomial basis and using Horner’s rule?

exr-ply-symmetric-a.title: B1
exr-ply-symmetric-a.html: Show that if x↦2c−x permutes the design and preserves the weights, then aj=c for every j and pj(2c−x)=(−1)jpj(x).

exr-ply-three-points.title: A1
exr-ply-three-points.html: Compute the monic orthogonal polynomials p0,p1,p2 for the design x=(−1,0,1) with unit weights from @eq-ply-recurrence, and check that their integer-scaled versions are the contrasts (−1,0,1) and (1,−2,1).

exr-ply-two-phase.title: B2
exr-ply-two-phase.html: Two straight lines meet at a known γ. Write the model in the basis 1,t,(t−γ)+, give the least squares estimate of the common value at γ and its variance, and the F statistic for equal slopes.

exr-ply-two-regressors.title: C2
exr-ply-two-regressors.html: For two regressors the analogue of Pd is the span of the monomials xrzs with r+s≤d. List an orthogonal basis ϕ1,ϕ2,… of it in a fixed order of nondecreasing total degree. The one-variable proof works because xpj expands in pj−1,pj,pj+1 alone; exhibit a design in R2 and an index i for which xϕi has a nonzero inner product with some ϕk, k<i−1, so that no scalar three-term recurrence generates the list. (Vector recurrences over a whole block of one total degree do exist; the single-variable bookkeeping is what fails.) Relate this to Chapter 44.

exr-ply-vandermonde-rank.title: A1
exr-ply-vandermonde-rank.html: Show that Xd=[1,x,…,xd] has full column rank if and only if the xi take at least d+1 distinct values, and deduce that a polynomial of degree n−1 through n points with distinct xi exists, is unique and interpolates exactly.

exr-ply-weierstrass.title: C1
exr-ply-weierstrass.html: The Weierstrass approximation theorem says that every continuous f on [a,b] is a uniform limit of polynomials. Using parts (a) and (c) of @prp-ply-instability, explain why this is not an argument for fitting high-degree polynomials to data. What does the theorem guarantee about the bias of the degree-d fit as d grows, and what about the variance?

exr-ply-which-basis.title: A2
exr-ply-which-basis.html: Three analysts fit a cubic spline with the same six knots, in the truncated power basis, in the local basis, and as free cubics under the continuity constraints. Which outputs agree exactly, which to rounding, and which disagree?

exr-ply-zeros.title: C1
exr-ply-zeros.html: Show that pj has j distinct real zeros, all strictly inside the range of the design. (Suppose it changes sign at only r<j interior points z1,…,zr, and consider ⟨pj,∏l(x−zl)⟩.)

lem-ply-shift.title: Multiplication by the argument is self-adjoint
lem-ply-shift.title_html: Multiplication by the argument is self-adjoint
lem-ply-shift.html: For polynomials f,g let (xf)(x)=xf(x). Then ⟨xf,g⟩=⟨f,xg⟩.

prp-ply-instability.title: Instability of a high-degree polynomial fit
prp-ply-instability.title_html: Instability of a high-degree polynomial fit
prp-ply-instability.html:
Let Xd=[1,x,…,xd] be the Vandermonde matrix of a design with at least d+1 distinct points, and let f^d be the least squares polynomial of degree d.

  1. (Conditioning.) If the design points are a sample from a distribution on [0,1] with density g, then n−1Xd⊤Xd→G almost surely, where Gjk=∫01xj+kg(x)dx. For the uniform density this limit is the (d+1)×(d+1) Hilbert matrix Gjk=1/(j+k+1), whose condition number grows exponentially in d.

  2. (Oscillation.) Interpolation by a polynomial of degree n−1 at n equally spaced points need not converge as n grows, even for a function that is analytic on the interval; the error can diverge. The failure is a property of the node placement, not of polynomials: at Chebyshev nodes the same interpolants converge geometrically.

  3. (Extrapolation.) Let x~d=(I−Md−1)xd be the part of the top power orthogonal to the lower ones. Then t↦Var{f^d(t)} is a polynomial of degree exactly 2d with leading coefficient σ2/‖x~d‖2, so Var{f^d(t)}σ2t2d⟶1‖x~d‖2as |t|→∞. Each extra degree therefore multiplies the standard error of the extrapolated curve by a further factor |t|, up to the constant ‖x~d‖/‖x~d+1‖.

  4. (Non-locality.) Changing one response yi by Δ changes the fitted curve at every t by Δℓi(t), where ℓi(t)=x(t)⊤(Xd⊤Xd)−1xi is itself a polynomial of degree at most d and never identically zero, so it vanishes at most d times: no observation can be given a purely local influence.

prp-ply-knots.title: Number, placement and basis
prp-ply-knots.html:
Fit a regression spline of degree d with interior knots κ1<⋯<κK inside the range of the design, and write MK for the projection onto the column space.

  1. (Number.) If X has full rank, trMK=d+1+K, so the leverages average (d+1+K)/n and 𝛍E‖(I−MK)Y‖2=σ2{n−(d+1+K)}+‖(I−MK)μ‖2. Increasing K decreases both the squared bias and the residual degrees of freedom; the price is the total variance of the fitted curve, σ2trMK=σ2(d+1+K), which rises by σ2 per knot. Knots buy bias reduction at one degree of freedom each.

  2. (Rank.) If each piece [κk,κk+1), k=0,…,K−1, and the last piece [κK,b] contain at least d+1 distinct design points, then X has full column rank. If some knot exceeds maxixi, its column is identically zero and X does not.

  3. (Placement.) For d=0 the variance of the fit on interval k is σ2/nk, with nk the number of design points there, so equalizing the counts minimizes the largest pointwise variance; quantile knots do that and equally spaced knots need not. For d≥1 the effect persists in the exact variance σ2x(t)⊤(X⊤X)−1x(t), which is large wherever an interval is sparsely occupied.

  4. (Basis.) The columns of @eq-ply-truncated are globally supported and increasingly parallel: beyond the last knot every one behaves like td, the angle between (x−κj)+d and (x−κk)+d tends to zero as κj−κk→0 (@exr-ply-knot-coalescence), and κ(X) grows with K. A basis of the same space whose members are each supported on d+1 consecutive intervals has a basis condition number — the worst ratio between the size of a coefficient vector and the size of the function it builds — bounded by a constant depending only on d, whatever the knots (de Boor, 2001). For a design with points in every basis function’s support, κ(X) then does not grow with K; without one nothing is claimed, and X can be singular.

thm-ply-recurrence.title: Existence, uniqueness and the three-term recurrence
thm-ply-recurrence.title_html: Existence, uniqueness and the three-term recurrence
thm-ply-recurrence.html:
Let d<m. The orthogonal polynomials of the design exist, are unique, and are generated by p−1=0,p0=1,pj+1(x)=(x−aj)pj(x)−bjpj−1(x),j=0,1,…,d−1,{#eq-ply-recurrence}

with aj=⟨xpj,pj⟩‖pj‖2,bj=‖pj‖2‖pj−1‖2 (j≥1),b0=0. Every ‖pj‖2 with j≤d is strictly positive.

thm-ply-spline-space.title: Dimension of the spline space and the truncated power basis
thm-ply-spline-space.title_html: Dimension of the spline space and the truncated power basis
thm-ply-spline-space.html:
Let d≥0 and let κ1<⋯<κK be interior knots of [a,b].

  1. Sd(κ) is a vector space of dimension d+1+K, and 1, t, …, td, (t−κ1)+d, …, (t−κK)+d{#eq-ply-truncated}

    is a basis of it.

  2. More generally, if the constraints imposed at κk are of order mk with −1≤mk≤d−1, the resulting space has dimension d+1+∑k=1K(d−mk), with basis the powers 1,…,td together with (t−κk)+r for r=mk+1,…,d and k=1,…,K.
